ownership.ticket_owner_identity: Immutable attempt_id + target/binding/revision/generation/epoch + process-instance UUID, boot ID, owner PID/start identity, exact child PID/start identity when spawned. Persist ownership before IO. PID alone and timestamps/heartbeat alone are insufficient.
ownership.acquire: SQLite BEGIN IMMEDIATE/CAS jointly excludes an active collection lease and active clear/clock operation. begin_collection and existing claim share this gate. Contending collection/collection and collection/clear-clock have exactly one durable winner; loser code collection_busy_or_maintenance or existing operation_busy_or_cooldown, no BMC IO.
ownership.deadline: All acquisition and at most one reservation retry share one monotonic180s total deadline. At exhaustion, stop issuing commands, terminate only the exact owned child, escalate kill if needed and reap within30s grace. Preserve fixed per-command bounds and output limits. No complete-success from expired work.
ownership.trusted_owner_probe: Manager.collection_owner_status(ticket) is the narrow local process-inspection boundary; returns running, unverifiable or dead_child_reaped. The last value requires proof of exact old process-instance death and old child absence/reaping with PID/start/boot association. Caller-supplied assertions, wall time or missing heartbeat are not proof. Unknown proof stays held.
ownership.recovery_api: recover_collection(bmc_ip,attempt_id) may release only a matching read lease after started_at+210s and trusted dead_child_reaped proof, under a short DB CAS. A live/unverifiable owner is not reclaimed. Owner persists until proof even if this holds the host. It never dispatches or reclaims a clear/clock mutation.
ownership.late_ticket: Old/expired/recovered ticket finish fails before row inserts/success. It cannot release or modify newer active_attempt_id/owner. Any release compares exact attempt_id and owner identity. Shared mutation outcome-unknown reconciliation retains its existing stronger rules unchanged.
